newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up but fundamental outlook bleak.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up but fundamental outlook bleak.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher on light technical-based trade buying, but not enough to brighten what many believe is a bleak picture for copper fundamentally.
The hedge funds stayed on the sidelines Tuesday, with most of the activity dominated by light consumer bargain hunting and smaller speculative shortcovering.
December delivery closed up 1.25 cents at 98.10 cents a lb, with September 1.15 cents higher at 97.80 cents. The spot month ended at 97.60 cents, up 1.10 cents.
"We got a little bounce today," said one trade broker. "It looked like a buying opportunity for them, but I think fundamentally we've got to look for lower prices. The LME stocks just keep going up."

LME warehouse stocks increased another 4,075 tonnes to 268,675 tonnes, the highest level since Sept 16, 1996. The cash-to-three-month contango was $7/$3 at 1442 EDT, the widest level since October 1996.

The broker attributed the stock increase to the backwardation that was in place until recently. "You have traders that were bringing in metal (from South America) and there was still an advantage to putting metal on the board when the market was in a back."
Now, the metal is likely to be shifted between LME and COMEX warehouses in Baltimore to exploit arbitrage differentials in the absence of physical demand, dealers said.
The COMEX spot price closed at a 0.60-cent premium to the LME cash price.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
